After two months spasms became again more frequent despite continuous treatment. Additionally, pseudobulbar dysarthria, mild spastic tetraparesis and generalised fasciculations developed. The EMG now showed signs of acute denervation (Fig. 1A) in upper and lower extremity muscles whereas the EMG interference pattern of the tongue was normal (Fig. 1B). CSF examination again revealed increased protein levels (1. 6 g/L) without pleocytosis. Motor and sensory nerve conduction were normal as was MRI. The patient died of pneumonia five years after onset after a gradually deteriorating tetraparesis and persisting stimulus-induced spasms.

extractions.quote: Progres sive encephalomyelitis with rigidity (PER) is a subacute polioencephalomyelitis within the spectrum of stiff-person syndromes (SPS) [1–6] which manifests with widespread rigidity, painful spasms, long tract signs and compromised brainstem function [1].

Progres sive encephalomyelitis with rigidity (PER) is a subacute polioencephalomyelitis within the spectrum of stiff-person syndromes (SPS) [1–6] which manifests with widespread rigidity, painful spasms, long tract signs and compromised brainstem function [1].
